title: Prove the fixed-core J caller joint cleanup support bound
body:
The phase-correct J caller now has a complete original-input cleanup and a scoped joint-tail lower bound. For q>=2 the exact all-q telescope `C R=F_k J` leaves only q native factors in R, even for arbitrary physical source monomials. Hence a complete native/monomial/binary-ADD tail needs total native arity plus ADD count at least `(2q+4)f`.

Under explicit paid full-bank scans, sublinear retained local tolls cannot hide a linear native-arity deficit in ADDs. With the additional equal-volume full-bank native-child normalization, including queried dirty helpers, the completed fixed-prefix mass is at least stock+4 and has no favorable proper-child moment. Unequal queried-bank volumes need a separate actual weighted bridge.

The package also supplies a conservative complete J caller: all public L-readers are scalar, every original field is restored to its actual `F_k J` output, and the full invoice is `H[2]=n^2+1, H[4]=2, H[6]=1`, mass=stock+16. Exact q2/q3 fixtures retain both inverse orders, all Gaussian f residues and every selected-native query. The all-q written derivations, finite checks and inherited C37/C38 resource/factory gates remain distinct.

Validation at `efb1b5a56a52967a4e94223bcdd03b209f4f09f5`:

- Registered Python 3.12 normal and optimized replay, with historical assertions preserved.

`research/phase-correct-j-handoff/README.md` gives the model, proofs, reproducible commands, source pins and next concrete question. `REPLAY-MAP.md` maps generation-time assertions to the fixed-witness verifier. Full attribution, inherited notices and Apache-2.0 license are retained. Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance is disclosed.

title: Research: dual-scale Norm exists for every odd-prime-power precision-blind pair (no new kappa)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Answers open question 1 of just-open [#4063](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4063): does every odd prime-power precision-blind `a=(1+p^{w-1},1)` on `(Z/p^w Z)^2` admit dual-scale Norm on the same two coordinates `(H'_1,D'_0)` into some reciprocal unit pair `(u,u^{-1})`?

**Yes**, with closed form `u=a0`:

- Dual scales `(s_{H1},s_{D0})=(a0^{-1},a0)` realize `F_{(a0,a0^{-1})}` with `(P')²=I`, so Theorem 1 of `weighted-wrapper-contract` makes two equal ordinary calls equal interchange `J` on all of `G×G`.
- No shared single-factor scale exists for any odd `p` and `w≥2` (`s²≡1` forces `s≡±1`, but `a0≢±1`).
- `a0` is **always** a unit quadratic residue mod `p^w` (`a0≡1 (mod p)`); dual-scale existence uses **invertibility**, not an explicit square root.

Algebraic for all odd `p`, `w≥2`. Certificate grid corroborates 15 pairs (`p∈{3,…,23}`, `w∈{2,…,5}`, `p^w≤2000`), with `#4063` cross-check `(3,2)→(7,4)`. Bank identity is exhaustive only for `(3,2)`; larger pairs use the closed form plus a lattice spot-check. **No Boolean meter inventory. No new kappa.** Selected κ stays `0.001672660197076918`.

## Task and overlap

- Package: `research/precision-blind-dual-scale-existence/`
- Tip: `9075bd0aa3fbde7a51c2839fa028707ab6add0f1`
- Base: `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90`
- Scope: **refined** — uniform existence/obstruction/square-class lemma answering #4063 OQ1

Closest prior: [#4063](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4063) (only `(3,2)` dual `(7,4)` + meters); [#4053](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4053); [#2950](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2950). Soft overlap vs #4063 ≈0.20–0.51 (not a meter retarget).

## Validation

```sh
python3.12 -I -B research/precision-blind-dual-scale-existence/verify.py
python3.12 -I -O -Werror -B research/precision-blind-dual-scale-existence/verify.py
python3.12 -I -B research/precision-blind-dual-scale-existence/independent.py
python3.12 -I -B research/precision-blind-dual-scale-existence/test_package.py
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/precision-blind-dual-scale-existence
```

Expected:

```text
PASS_PRECISION_BLIND_DUAL_SCALE_EXISTENCE pairs=15 primes=[3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19, 23] widths=[2, 3, 4, 5] single_factor=0 square=always dual_scales=inv crosscheck_4063=(7,4) boolean_meters=false no_new_kappa
PASS_INDEPENDENT_PRECISION_BLIND_DUAL_SCALE_EXISTENCE pairs=15 single_factor=0 square=always dual_scales=inv crosscheck_4063=(7,4) boolean_meters=false no_new_kappa
PASS_PRECISION_BLIND_DUAL_SCALE_EXISTENCE_PACKAGE_TESTS groups=6
PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/precision-blind-dual-scale-existence outcome=completed
```

Default verify is read-only. Admission uses `need()` and still fires under `-O`.

## Credit

Credit [#4063](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4063) for the `(3,2)` dual-scale Boolean invoice and OQ1; [#4053](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4053); Jerry Chen (@CubeJerry) / [#2950](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2950) for Theorem 1 / formula (5) / precision-blind family. Prepared by Wentao Li ([VictorLiwentao](https://github.com/VictorLiwentao), [@Is__Victor](https://x.com/Is__Victor)) with substantial AI assistance, under Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions / limitations

1. Does the same dual-scale reciprocal construction extend to precision-blind lists of length `n>2` with middle coordinates forced to `±1`?
2. A fully charged Boolean inventory for a further `(p,w)` would need a new closed form or fixture obligation — leave-alone policy blocks thin meter retargets of #4063/#4053.

title: Prove coupled E8 coordinate floors and the 28-neighbor partial-quotient case
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Conditional on the retained written premises from pending same-author
[PR3755](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3755), proves
term-count-independent **COPY ≥ 72** for new two-sided exact full-E8
factorizations `PQᵀ = G/2` with left space inside `C + Kδ_v`, where `C` is
the eight-dimensional root-evaluation code. The dense binary COPY table is
fixed before scalar reduction, and transposes are ordinary.

The load-bearing premises are PR3755's singleton classification, rank-at-most-nine
theorem and coordinate-pair classification. Vendored hashes and finite
certificate replays preserve those dependencies; they do not independently
validate the written proofs. The low-budget partial-quotient argument also
uses PR3166 Theorem A, recorded as partially reviewed in the upstream ledger.

The reusable step is an **actual-basis coupling lemma**. The only unpaid
singleton/hole state marks a coordinate of the actual equality basis as `−1`;
the free-pivot cut forces that same coordinate to be zero. The argument does
not replace the given basis with a conveniently chosen minimum basis.

The resulting floors cover:

- **Every full actual coordinate extension** `col(Q) = C + D_A`, in
  characteristic zero, with each exceptional left ray occurring at most once.
- **Raw coordinate-pair inclusion** `col(Q) ⊂ C + span(δ_a,δ_b)` over every
  characteristic different from two.
- **Raw arbitrary partial quotients supported on at most 28 neighbors of v**,
  and supports of at most 13 coordinates whose binary label span excludes
  `u_v`, in characteristic zero.
- **Inherited strict-floor corollary:** any actual right space of dimension
  at least 24, in characteristic zero, under the same exceptional-left-ray
  condition. Its one-sided slack comes from PR2962's existing size relaxation.

Raw inclusion results handle proportional merging and the actual rank drops.
All actual spaces/ranks first discard zero-factor terms. Ambient inclusion
alone is not substituted for full actual right-space equality.

The partial-quotient extension uses two new sharp word bounds: nonroot
weight-eight words need **27 neighbor deletions**, and root weight-seven
words need **29**. An explicit 24-neighbor word already refutes the stronger
eligible-root-only classification. The invoice proof nevertheless reaches
28 by bounding the whole coefficient-space support at low basis budget;
it permits the nonroot weight-eight words appearing at 27. A further sharp
nonroot low-word threshold is 55, so the next 29–54 cases involve root
normals only.

For normalized actual ranks `(9,n)`, `n ≥ 10`, the floor gives
`Σ ρᵢ^q ≥ 1 + 8^q + 7·9^q` for `0 < q ≤ 1`. An eleven-term rank-(9,10)
fixture attains this. The expression and concavity method credit adamgall's
PR2062; the new result is its coupled-space coverage. A noncoordinate
partial quotient also attains COPY 72 and survives normalization on both
sides. A normalized rank-(9,17) eighteen-term fixture has an actual basis
bill of 73 but COPY 72, showing that the single rebate is sharp. Raw-rank
padding controls explain the normalization requirement.

Only `research/e8-coupled-coordinate-floor/` is added. This does not close
general C′, G1-MFREE, arbitrary partial reader spaces of dimensions 10–23,
masked/punctured decoders, or a new κ.

## Task and overlap

Base `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90`, priority revision 6.
`TASK.json` records the handoff-driven change from `complex-rank-shape-decoder`
to this scoped structural obstruction. This is an off-card partial result,
not the card's construction acceptance gate; maintainers may give it lower
priority than current priority-card work.

[PR3154](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3154)'s
ARCHITECT / RL-s1 compensation questions and
[PR3755](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3755)'s higher-rank
residual motivate this work. PR3755 already proves the one-coset budget and
both-ranks-at-most-nine case; it does not supply the coupled rank-(9,10+)
consumers proved here. Its exact geometry and written premises are retained
with hashes, so no pending commit is required for replay.

Arham-Tahir64's [PR2798](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2798)
already proves charged-pure compensation on its fixed P112 completion. Target rank
eight alone is not the distinction. The additional scope here is full P120,
every actual coordinate extension, and the normalization-stable partial spaces.
The L120 programme in PR3074/3191 is adjacent; no conditional completion of
that programme is used as a premise for these two-sided theorems.

The read-only October 19, 11:19 UTC refresh screened 177 updated open/closed
PRs since 01:44 UTC, followed plausible matches to their pinned primary
sources, and read all 53 changed comments/replies in six relevant Discussions.
Those threads were fully paginated: 931 comments and 158 replies were
captured. Main, PR3154/3755 heads and all four live input pins were unchanged.
No matching completion or dependency counteraudit appeared in that coverage.
Other threads, private work and arbitrary PR diffs remain outside this
bounded check; it is not a novelty guarantee. No public claim was posted.

The closest new work is Clear1nsight's
[PR3973](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3973), bounding
residual-rank-seven normal directions under a common P112 cut, and
[PR4012](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4012), strengthening
an eleven-piece P112 support-incidence floor to 178. These provide adjacent
geometry and historical caller exclusions, not the full-P120 actual-basis
compensation or COPY invoice proved here.
[PR3951](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3951) audits inherited
capacity/A2 inputs; it does not validate the weighted root-swap or PR3755
premises on which this package depends.

The changed-32-port search in Discussion1587 was released without a sub-64
construction. Source-level inspection also distinguishes PR3876's rank-112
identity and full-port tariff from this rank-eight Gram target and line-label
tariff; the new fixed-P112 gauge screens retain their different target and bill.

## Validation

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/e8-coupled-coordinate-floor
```

- Exact root/parabolic/Fourier inputs, 109 unit minors, 61,320 root/character
  checks and all 49 strict-dimension cases through two dynamic programs.
- Relative bound 27 through 15,575,280 parabolic comparisons and a separate
  complete scalar-kernel method. Root-low bound 29 through all 14,400 ordered
  root pairs and a separate 10,851-plane fixed-pivot exhaustion. Nonroot-low
  bound 55 through 30,480 parabolic/pivot cases and a separate full-support
  scalar-stratum algorithm.
- Exact products, actual ranks, normalization and binary tariffs over Q,
  F3, F5 and F7; 60 actual equality bases and 7,200 cuts; noncoordinate
  equality fixtures and genuine product/compensation failure controls.
- Registered replay, committed-byte/source-history checks, official export
  integrity, optimized Git-free replay, artifact/bytecode controls,
  attribution preflight and `git diff --check` pass on the frozen candidate.

The two relative-cut implementations share the Weyl/parabolic reduction
for the complement-character branch. The separate AI-assisted audit sampled
that branch; it did not independently exhaust it.

Five Init-only Lean 4.21.0 declarations check the additive contradiction and
critical-state/actual-basis arithmetic, with warnings as errors. Full E8
instantiation, geometric dependencies, field transfer and theorem assembly
remain written. Internal AI-assisted review is not independent human
certification. Hosted CI and repository-wide builds have not been run.
Lean RSS observations are sampled; sub-second runs do not establish a
measured peak-memory bound.
The candidate contains one focused commit.

## Credit

The singleton-ray and all-odd pair inputs credit conorholds' PR3755;
the weighted root-swap, Fourier and parabolic inputs credit PR3166.
DreamingOfClouds' PR2962 supplies the inherited prefix-counting relaxation,
and PR3154 supplies the scoped C′ / RL-s1 obligations. adamgall's PR2062
supplies the concave profile and argument. Arham-Tahir64's PR2798 compensation result is
distinguished above. Earlier E8, projection, compatible-independence and
all-odd rank-witness credits are retained in `NOTICE.md` and the vendored
source. Assistance and licensing are disclosed there and in `TASK.json`.

## Open next questions

Extend the actual-basis cut argument to unrestricted partial right spaces
of dimensions 10–23; account for mixed weight-seven words starting at 29
neighbor corrections; and formalize the E8/linear-functional and invoice
bridges. The 24- and 29-coordinate controls prevent silently reusing the
stronger classifications beyond their proved boundaries.

title: Bound sparse feedback volume by conditioning and the native entropy jump
body:
The selected coupled boundary requires `(C_f x+B_f y/2,y)`. PR4009's full-array pass bound does not by itself charge sparse updates. This package proves a separate arithmetic-volume/conditioning tradeoff using an Ailon-style preconditioned quasi-entropy:

`8 K S + Re(Delta_Q) >= fV/2`.

Here `S` is the total number of updated coordinates, `K` bounds every full formal machine prefix condition number, and `Delta_Q` is the explicit entropy jump across the sole native call. Arbitrary sparse feedback, variable mask sizes, restored arbitrary dirty auxiliaries and clean returned auxiliaries are allowed. Monomial routing/scaling is granted free for the lower bound; its actual physical invoice remains extra.

When the target child runs before arithmetic, preceded only by payload-preserving monomials, its jump is zero: **`S >= fV/(16K)`**. Thus uniformly bounded-condition child-first sparse adapters still require order `fV` arithmetic. A general interleaved call retains its actual jump; unrestricted conditioning, general sparse algorithms and complete supplier admission remain open. No new kappa or selected frontier change is claimed.

The scoped contribution is the analytical block preconditioner `J_xy=C_f^-1 B_f`, its exact endpoint value, the dimension-free complex coordinate-shear bound, and explicit native-cut accounting. Ordinary determinant and unpreconditioned quasi-entropy miss the triangular correction. The proof includes clean auxiliaries without imposing their off-domain nonzero-input behavior. Allow the selected target195/donor521 boundary to use coordinate-orbit blocks of unequal volumes, with a separate partial-fusion choice `k` on each block. The two native child ranks become `f+k` and `f-k`; the exact middle transfer is `B_K y/2`.

For any fixed block-wide feedback adapter with restored donor and arbitrary dirty helpers, at least `k+1` shears are necessary. Relative to the original one ADD, let `W = sum(block_volume * k)`. Extra arithmetic is at least `W`, while the rank-only recursive saving is at most `A delta f^(-alpha) W`, where `delta = 2-2^(1-alpha)` and `A` is one fixed coefficient in matching arithmetic units. Extends the selected-source rank-two macro-fusion screen with an exact operator audit of its named phase-B witness. The rank-one recipes `0→2` and `2→252` compose to the pinned rank-two recipe `0→252`: exact Gaussian-dyadic matrices agree on all 512 basis columns, with matching canonical operator digest.

The intervening ADD still blocks direct replacement. In the forward trace, `L195_out = D x + (1/2) B y`, where `D=BA` and `y=L521`. In the backward trace, the caller also observes the intermediate value through `L521_out = y - (1/2) A x`. The available rank-two recipe emits only `D x`; it does not supply either missing block. A separate rank-one-equivalent tap produces the profile `[2,1]`, whose ideal recursive charge `2^(1-a)+1` is greater than the original `[1,1]` charge `2` for `0<a<1`, before conversion and restoration costs.

Across both orientations, 35 endpoint-matching candidates remain interrupted by scalar work, and all 100 candidate/add-operand instances lack a reusable same-key transition. This is a positive exact composition identity and a negative result for the selected single-output replacement contract. No multi-output provider, new supplier or κ improvement is claimed; selected κ remains `0.001672660197076918`.

## Task and overlap

Base: canonical main `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90`. Task `complex-rank-shape-decoder`, narrowed to successive same-register rank-one climbs and their intervening scalar operation. The fresh overlap refresh covered 734 open PRs and 2,596 Discussions with complete pagination. The query surfaced [PR #3998](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3998), a different staged544 scalar-ADD graph. [PR #1836](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1836) and its [`complex-heterogeneous-child-interface` audit](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/main/research/complex-heterogeneous-child-interface/README.md) study simultaneous unequal-rank pairing, not this sequential pair with an observable intermediate. Novelty remains scoped to this contract.

## Validation

The registered package passed its metadata/source-pin check and normal plus optimized CPython 3.12 replays:

```sh
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/complex-rank2-macro-fusion-screen --check-only
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/complex-rank2-macro-fusion-screen
```

The replay checks both source orientations, the complete 597-event `L195` windows, the exact 512-column child composition, stored operator digests, nonzero ADD taps, same-key reuse census, and wrong-rank/source-removal controls. Evidence and hashes are in `RESULT.json`.

## Credit

Credit Cinna Davis / PR #1836 and Adam Gall's `complex-heterogeneous-child-interface` audit for the simultaneous unequal-rank census and reciprocal-encoding classification; credit the selected PR #1094 provider lineage and its pinned source audit. Prepared by Gonzalo Mier with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Apache-2.0; no independent human review claimed.

## Open next questions

Only a changed multi-output/tap provider could absorb this witness's intermediate while retaining the exact operator. The pinned recipes expose one vector output, and the separated rank-two-plus-rank-one profile is already more expensive. A multi-output vector-decoder test would need its own exact input/output contract and complete copy, frame, precision and restoration invoice; it belongs to the separate vector-decoding proposal rather than an expansion of this stopped direct-fusion screen.

title: Negative result: A4 four-role target diag([a],[b],[c],[d]) has exact minimum 8 (no seven-call word; radical-rank proof); no kappa
body:
## Statement

In the formal `F2[A4]` four-role model of #2116, the target `T = diag([a],[b],[c],[d])` has **exact minimum 8**. Here `a=(123)`, `b=(124)`, `c=(12)(34)` and `d=ab=(13)(24)`. There is no seven-call word, so the model gives no cross-role paid-call saving for this target. No `kappa` claim.

| Length | Status | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| 1-5 | impossible | written proof (Lemmas 1-2); also both joins |
| 6 | impossible | exhaustive joins A and B (reproduces #2116); not covered by the written lemmas |
| 7 | impossible | written proof (Lemmas 1-2); also both exhaustive joins |
| 8 | realized | direct word, replayed exactly on all 48 basis inputs |

The kinds of evidence differ. Length 7 and lengths up to 5 are excluded by a written proof. Length 6 is excluded by a finite exhaustive certificate. Length 8 is an explicit construction. None of this is a multiplication theorem, a supplier result or a `kappa` change.

**Written proof.**
- Lemma 1 (C3 determinant): `det` over `F2[C3]` gives `n_a = n_b (mod 3)`.
- Lemma 2 (radical rank, new here):
  - Write `b = a^2 d`. Every word then factors as `W = A * prod(I + C_k^-1 (d+1) N_k C_k)`, with `A` in `GL4(F2[<a>])`.
  - `F2[<a>]` meets the radical `J` only in 0, so `A` is the unique lift `diag(a, a^2, 1, 1)`. The defect is `diag(1, d, c, d)`.
  - A twisted functional `Phi: J/J^2 -> F4` satisfies `Phi(r y s) = aug(r) Phi(y) psi(s)`. It turns the defect into a sum of `n_b` matrices of rank at most 1 that has rank 3. So `n_b >= 3`. Base `b` gives `n_a >= 3` in the same way.
- Together the two lemmas exclude `(2,5)` and `(5,2)` at length 7, and every length up to 5. Length 6 would need `(3,3)`.

The per-label floor `n_b >= rank_F4 Phi(L^-1 T - I)` holds in this `F2[A4]` alphabet for any number of roles. Whether it extends beyond `A4 = V x| C3` is open question 2; it is not claimed here.

## Milestone and decision informed

- Milestone: a local formal module. There is no supplier, no native conversion and no `kappa`.
- Question decided: the length-7 slice that #2116 names as its open question.
- Decision: the A4 four-role endpoint gives no formal saving, so this target gives no reason to price a native conversion of `F2[A4]` calls. The package extends the existing direct-optimal pattern of the formal finite-group family (Q8 #2047/#2248, SL2(F3) #2010) to one more target. It changes no current lead, supplier or selected result.

## Base and pins

- Base: `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90`, under priority revision 6. Canonical main had not moved at submission.
- Pinned input: #2116's `RESULT.json` (git blob and sha256 in `SOURCES.json`).
- Package: `research/a4-seven-call-radical-rank/`, 7 new files. Nothing else is touched.

## Reproduce

```bash
python3 -I -B research/a4-seven-call-radical-rank/verify.py
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/a4-seven-call-radical-rank --check-only
```

The verifier uses only the standard library and compiles two C joins with `cc -O3`. It ends with `PASS_A4_FOUR_ROLE_EXACT_MINIMUM_EIGHT`, which reports:
- Direct word: 8 calls, 48/48 basis inputs.
- Lemma: defect rank 3 in both bases.
- Each join: 6,655,830 minimal-length-3 classes expanded and 1,597,399,200 children looked up, with no word of length up to 7.

The second command prints `PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS`. A run takes about 80-90 s wall time with about 369 MB peak RSS (Python 3.14.4, gcc 15.2.0). The generic runner also passed under a private Python 3.12.15 (`PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE`).

## Certificates and negative controls

- **Two separately implemented exhaustive joins** (same AI-assisted session).
  - Join A uses 4x4 matrices of 12-bit masks, left-inverse enumeration and a GF(2)-linear incremental hash.
  - Join B uses graded 12 x 16-bit coefficient matrices, right-inverse enumeration, a left-multiplication `P<=3` build and a nonlinear hash.
  - Both find `P<=3` = 1/240/41,920/6,655,830 (total 6,697,991). This matches #2116's pinned `right_distinct_exact_states`, and the verifier asserts it.
- **Verifier checks of the proof.** Every proof step is checked numerically: the factor split for all 120 idempotents, `dim J = 9`, unique lifts, the twisted bimodule law on all 512 elements of `J`, `Phi(J^2) = 0`, the step-5 identity on random words, and the determinant formula on random words.
- **Negative and positive controls.**
  - Each of the 8 single-call omissions of the direct word is rejected.
  - The label mutation (final call `b -> a`) is rejected.
  - Three-output control `diag([a],[b],[c],1)`: the defect rank drops to 2, and both joins find `(3,3)` 6-words that Python replays exactly.
  - Planted 7-words (2 per join) are found and replayed.

## Scope, assumptions, unresolved obligations

- The model is inherited unchanged from #2116: 240 rank-one idempotent factors `D_N(g) = I + ([g]+[1])N` with `g` in `{a,b}`, unit prices, four roles, dirty inputs, no workspace and exact equality of every formal coefficient.
- Free scalar `GL4(F2)` mixing and role permutations do not help. Conjugating them to the left leaves a scalar factor that augmentation forces to be `I`.
- Length 6 is excluded only by exhaustive search. A written proof of it is open question 1.
- Unpriced (unknown, not zero): native conversion, restored workspace, a physical caller, chronology, hosting, precision, recursive transfer and supplier admission.

## Search record

- Domain: all words of length up to 7 over the 240-factor alphabet. They are organized as `X·Y` and `X·f·Y`, with `X` and `Y` in `P<=3`.
- Coverage is complete in each join. Hashing is deterministic.
- There is no C3 or coset pruning and no early exit. Sampling is used only in the controls.
- No timeouts and no memory limits were hit.

## Credit and concurrent work

- The model, alphabet, direct word, C3 screen and the original length-6 exclusion come from #2116 (`research/a4-commutator-four-role-seed-dcbf`, GitHub @1337isnot1337, commit author Cinna Davis, head `19cdf74a`). This PR answers that package's named open question.
- Prior untwisted `J/J^2` arguments, all by @1337isnot1337: Q8 in #2047 and #2248, and the abelian rational-frame floor in #2085. #2085 is the closest analogue of the rank-count step.
- Open #3893 (@1337isnot1337) is a concurrent, different rank floor for S3.
- To our knowledge (a search of `research/*/README.md` and open PRs at the base), three ingredients are new: the semisimple split in a non-local group algebra, the twisted functional, and the use of both bases together with the C3 determinant.

Claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2095#discussioncomment-19037476

## Review provenance

The package was reviewed by four independent AI review passes in the same loop: reproducibility, adversarial mathematics, provenance and referee. They raised only minor issues, all of which were addressed in one revision. The math pass also checked the result with its own construction of A4 and its own exact BFS for length up to 6. No human review is claimed.

## Attribution

Prepared by Sagar Thakrar (@thakrarsagar) with substantial AI assistance from Claude (Anthropic, Claude Opus 5.5 via Claude Code) in an automated research loop.

title: Audit staged544 native phases and expose the binary-inverse lift defect
body:
PR3945 changes 26 terminal frames per staged544 provider. A binary frame/owner audit cannot establish the signed native action. This independently checks every promoted cold residual and all five genuinely changed warp interfaces per provider, including both warp directions and old/new interfaces: **40 unique interfaces, 144 source occurrences, 20,480 complete basis-column equalities**. All pass. Another 47 warp-record changes per provider only shift chronological indices.

The pairing of framed arithmetic with finite symplectic geometry gives a useful source-bound warning: for the actual map `G=[1,2,8,32,44,128,59,66,489]`, the canonical lift of the binary inverse satisfies `K_(G inverse) K_G = Z_256`, changing the signs of 256 basis coordinates despite an identity binary map. The author's correct adjoint passes; this is a phase-discipline witness, **not an author bug**. The correction is a nonconstant Pauli character, not just global phase.

The new standard-library verifier uses exact Gaussian integers and independent serialized-recipe decoding; it executes no predecessor compiler/checker. Frozen predecessor code is used only for optional reference generation. Fourteen phase, rank, basis and coverage mutations reject. Actual dirty-state coverage is equality on all 512 basis columns at each local interface, with every output coefficient and global phase checked. Whole-program dirty cleanup, changed scalar-transition classes and supplier admission are separate.

Frozen release crosslinks are also checked from included raw bytes: both actual word hashes, native recipe inventories, final package manifest and reported release receipt. The full native recipe payload and release execution are not replayed. The author's disclosed frozen-spec corrections and reused successful prefixes remain explicit. title: Prove source-bound prime supply for the many-axis tensor caller
body:
## Result and boundary

This supplies the odd, pairwise-coprime source lengths explicitly left open by #4024, bound to #3935's actual `TensorPlan.production_axis`. The old source08/Cinna Davis selector uses `log(t)>8d`; that premise does not port to the newer `D=Theta(p^.997), ell=Theta(p^.003)` family. This is a changed parameter-regime implication, not a failure of the old lemma.

Write D for actual scalar axes and d=D+1. For `ell>=2^32`, `2<=d<=ell^334`, and `target_halo+2w<=2^(ell-3)`, each interior interval `(t(1-1/(3d)),t(1-1/(4d))]`, for t equal to either target scale, contains at least D primes. Ordered distinct selections satisfy all three source axis guards and full `T/S<3/2<2`. The separate period premise is explicit; arbitrary halo is not admitted by prime abundance.

`PROOF.md` derives that deliberately conservative effective domain from [Fiori–Kadiri–Swidinsky, arXiv2206.12557v2 Corollary22](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2206.12557v2), an imported analytic theorem. It includes the two-scale ordering/product argument and a uniform fixed-tape trial-division/list construction with `O(r² ell²+D ell)` steps and `O(D ell+ell)` visited backing for this prime producer, r=2^ell, including scratch erasure and head returns. Under the retained caller laws its setup is `2^o(p)=o(V)`. Existing CRT metadata retains its own separately paid bill; an explicit p cutoff requires fixed growth/halo constants.

The executed program is a **host-integer finite reference**, `encoded_execution=false`. It authenticates five local source exports and extracts the complete source axis-method AST using a semantic Count adapter. It does not execute encoded predecessor arithmetic, giant primes, a production tensor or native supplier. The uniform machine construction is written, not executed.

## Validation

Only `research/many-axis-prime-supply/` is added:19 files, one canonical-parent commit `726c9a3a1dc58d2b1223dd681eb712255be407c1`; public tree equals the locally tested tree.

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/many-axis-prime-supply
```

Five mixed-scale/nonmonotone finite cases, full source guards, products and encoded source/flag hashes pass. The separate checker imports no primary executable and uses Eratosthenes plus exact rational/integer predicates and symbolic threshold inequalities. The primary has8 internal controls; the separate suite checks50 expected rejections and5 positives, including strict equalities, actual D versus d, same/mixed-scale duplicate primes, composites, ownership, authenticated AST and typed/corrupted receipts. No giant target or axis list is constructed.

CPython3.12.14 registered replay, exact-public-commit byte/source-history check and official export/check pass. All three standalone commands pass normally and with `-O` from a fully0444/0555, Git-free20-file official export with empty PATH/PYTHONPATH. Every file retains bytes, modes and inode. Archive SHA256 `ce3232e7644d18733b9013654c52f401947d1fe219c80e77074c6b2fcdd2b468`. [Hosted exact-head run39237273642](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/39237273642) passes:265 onboarding tests (11skips), only this package selected, all three commands on CPython3.12.15 and unchanged committed inputs. Logs bind this head to test merge70c5c6f2 against canonical20ecf289. Finite execution does not reprove the imported analytic theorem or formalize the full multiplication theorem.

## Selection, credit and remaining work

Handoff-first changed `supplier-boundary-audit` scope; original card, attempted baseline command and missing sparse inventory dependency are recorded in `TASK.json`. [Canonical claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4024#issuecomment-6264858503). Canonical main `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90`, priority6, catalogue and selected record refreshed unchanged before submission. Source #4024 `e99297be6749518a1b5b85cd129ecaf204d26c63`; #3935 `240597ed313fc2854c0462b23c89dc3bae72aaf5`. Entry overlap:729 completely paginated open PR bodies including drafts, repository helper and retained prime-supply predecessors; pre-submission latest100-body delta through #4028 and bounded live handoffs/source comments. Broader Discussion/closed/code coverage remains partial. Jose Manuel's [prospective numerical recovery lane](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/3664#discussioncomment-19036660) is separate.

Credit Jose Manuel/jmbarrancoml's tensor interface, Tekalign/tekuuu's CRT converter and explicit premise, Cinna Davis's old-domain selector transfer, Chafik Boukhalfa/#1786 and JosieElliston's prior fine-prime transfer audit, Fiori–Kadiri–Swidinsky's analytic theorem, Harvey–van der Hoeven/source08 trial-division construction and Agarwal–Cooley CRT algebra. Frozen READMEs retain the OpenAI manuscript, Douglas Colkitt, RaD/hipotures and deeper runtime lineage. No invention of trial division or the generic explicit-PNT method is claimed. ToikY with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance and separate AI proof/test contexts; Apache-2.0. No independent human or formal-kernel acceptance.

title: Derive QQ16 ordered-query residual and restricted Schur obstruction
body:
The borrowed-current-Y shortcut to PR3985 removes 104 negative normalizers but omits the actual prefix correction. This package derives that correction from the pinned full-recovery source and rules out the proposed scalar or 8/16 one-owner-route parallel repair.

The missing query is `Q2(X_T) − M21 Q1(Y)`, where `M21=(1/4) Σ r_p r_pᵀ[g2,p g1,p]`. Constants collapse this operator to `13I`, but the single character `v=1` separates all **104** actual ordered routes. The diagonal `(0,0)` sends that character to **52** distinct characters with coefficient `1/4`; it is not `13I`. Every eight-component query is attainable from actual current Y supported on A, and the A response is injective, so the witness applies to this caller boundary.

The exact restricted optimum is **104 parallel branches**, each allowing arbitrary constant 8×8 channel mixing and one common linear owner permutation. This is **not a native-child lower bound** or a general circuit barrier. Sequential route reuse, paid harmonic projections and changed producers remain outside the model. No native saving, supplier admission or improved κ is claimed.

Evidence in `research/qq16-query-schur/`:
- All 104 literal prefix rows and the complete ordered residual checked over independent current arrays.
- Exact character witness, current-query surjection and response injectivity.
- All 104 borrowed-Y hole maps checked against the full phase polynomial: the bypass has valid frames but wrong values.
- Complete typed receipt, immutable source authentication before inherited execution, normal/optimized Git-free read-only replay, source/manifest/receipt/overwrite rejection controls, and registered package verification.

title: Prove a shared-frame normalization gate for QQ16 template lifts
body:
The fixed104-owner-route repair of PR4003's ordered QQ16 residual cannot save its104 native normalizations by changing one shared input-query frame. This PR proves that gate for every positive integer λ, including common frames that mix planes, under the explicitly separately normalized branch contract and prescribed phase-normalizer tariff. For `0≤a≤10/13`, the minimum formal native moment is the unchanged `104 λ^(1-a)`; every nonzero common polar perturbation is strictly worse.

The source certificate partitions the104 pulled-back defect directions into12 independent groups, the minimum possible given their rank9 span. This gives the all-parameter inequality `Σ rank(defect) ≥104λ+80 rank(Δ)`. Symmetric image intersections and concavity prove the result; no lifted-frame census is used. The bounded seed47 balanced-greedy construction found the exact partition on its first restart. For λ=1 and `0≤a≤1/2`, the stronger nonzero-change lower bound is >144 versus baseline104.

The104 source owner routes and the F16 output frame are fixed. A different owner decomposition, shared/joint branch normalization, changed producer/output frame, paid address-valued scans or other alphabets remain outside scope. The tariff is an accounting model, not a wall-clock or bit/tape lower bound. Retention, routing, helpers, restoration, precision and actual outer consumption are still separate nonnegative obligations, granted free only in the favorable lower-bound screen. No new κ, physical supplier admission or full multiplication theorem is claimed.

Validation: registered Python3.12 replay of all four commands; exact full Z4 source frames and owners; a separate no-inherited-code row/character implementation; 15,834 small rank-one cases; 4,164 symmetric-pair guards; a genuinely plane-mixing λ=2 fixture;16 behavioral rejections. title: research: classify rational rank-one gauges in P112 fit
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Classifies every rational rank-one basis update `G=I+uv^T` whose left and right supports have union of size exactly four, on every four-channel block of the PR3335 rank-34 P112 factorization. Diagonal similarity reduces each support pattern to rational overlap products; exact affine equations and hyperplane avoidance classify every source/inverse diagonal-zero cell. This is the complete rank-one family on a four-channel block, not arbitrary `GL4(Q)`, rank-two updates or update sequences.

## Result

The exact classifier checks 1,294 support/diagonal-flag cells: 373 feasible and 921 obstructed, yielding 365 distinct rational source/inverse support pairs. Pricing those pairs on all 46,376 channel quadruples checks 16,927,240 cases. The minimum invoice remains 224 on every quadruple; no strict improvement occurs. The full-support subset is worse (minimum 228). No kappa or supplier change is claimed.

title: Prove sharp fixed-support unary-query bounds with restored dirty banks
body:
## Summary

- Prove a sharp `2n` query bound for applying a fixed carrier squared to `n` independent data banks while restoring any finite number of arbitrary dirty helper banks. Two queries per output attain the bound.
- Allow free invertible bank mixing over the internal-swap algebra for the balanced order-four carrier. A separate quartic theorem proves the same bound with scalar bank mixing.
- Keep the paid-scan counterexample alongside the theorem: additional ADDRESS-valued operations can produce two full chirps with zero native queries, but require `6mf` complete ADD scans plus paid swaps, signs and addressing.

Package and detailed proofs: [fixed-support-unary-query-bounds](https://github.com/RossRichardson/integer-mult-bounds/tree/9124007ea9029a9a3b88898bb4c350ddb27ffa58/research/fixed-support-unary-query-bounds).

## Scope and limits

The main theorem is over a characteristic-zero field containing `i`, with fixed support, balanced `N²=-I`, carrier `A=(N⊗I)S`, one-bank `A` or `A⁻¹` queries and exact restoration of every extra bank. The quartic companion requires all four eigencharacters of `z⁴+1` and scalar bridges; it does not inherit the larger swap-algebra alphabet.

The quantified lower bounds are written proofs. Finite exact witnesses verify actual constituents and noncommuting word identities, including all 32 sign choices of one five-query word and meaningful order/phase/omission controls. They are not exhaustive word searches or formal-kernel proofs. Changing supports, permitted operators or restoration changes the premises. Native pricing and physical implementation remain separate; no new kappa, selected-frontier improvement or full multiplication theorem is claimed.

## Test plan

Publication head: `9124007ea9029a9a3b88898bb4c350ddb27ffa58`.

- [x] `python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/fixed-support-unary-query-bounds` — registered normal and optimized replay, exact Gaussian/full group-algebra identities, quartic and scan fixtures, defect controls.

The package uses Python 3.12 and the standard library. Replay requires no private checker, Git checkout or external local research directory.

The original fixed-support proof, quartic companion and scan construction are retained with a separate independent AI derivation and portable replay. The causal factorization, image/row-space and character-rank methods credit eumemic's [retained PR288 source](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90/research/abelian-cayley-metric-scope/sources/pr288-README.md) and Ali Romman's [PR468](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/07a78bf335b0b5039a1fecd7cd74a0fe1d1605ea/research/bit-three-register-lower-bound/README.md). The first literal sequential candidate handed off by #3975 has an exact finite fusion: replace its two rank-one target calls by the rank-two endpoint recipe and implement the intervening donor transfer with four rational array ADDs and six monomial source maps. The transfer is B=((1+i)I+(1-i)P)/2, where P is the explicit signed-XOR Pauli with xor224/sign-mask96. The positive finite identity has a precise lifting cost: at tensor multiplicity f, a direct read-only-donor monomial accumulation needs exactly 2^f transfer channels. The literal array bill is at least V·2^f, not a constant native-adapter invoice. Its internal physical ADDs are a new macro contract; the inherited common-frame scalar-word checker is not claimed to admit the new sequence.

Two exact donor-retiming alternatives also fail their optimistic recursive budgets. Immediate restoration increases normalized charge by 2^(1-a); deferral to the donor's next actual child forces width3 and increases it by 3^(1-a)-1. Both are positive for 0<a<1. A separate operator-algebra proof excludes one arbitrary operator call plus coordinate-uniform scalar mixing: the required blocks I,B,C span dimension3, witnessed by determinant(1+i)/4. title: Bind one selected Toom candidate to its dirty-input interface
body:
## Result

The first nine-climb group from the event-window model used in Gonzalo Mier's #3974 is an invertible 4,608-dimensional linear operator on nine independent dirty payloads. This package binds that actual group to its exact frames, incoming forms and serialized Clifford recipes, then rejects precise same-width Toom-only interfaces, including rational coefficient encoding and rational output decoding.

The first eight registers `546,560,547,568,548,558,549,570` climb from frame 0 to `[459]`; register 464 climbs from frame 0 to `[75]`. Their actual incoming forms have a nine-by-nine identity minor. The selected receipt explicitly covers every arbitrary data/helper column, and the verifier proves the actual entry prefix is invertible: 7,344 shears, 56 nonzero scales, 464 typed frame adapters and 240 invertible monomial pre-wrappers; no clears or copies. The two 512-dimensional operators are reconstructed on all 1,024 basis columns, with exact global phase, halving and Gram matrices.

- A fixed-factor Toom module receives at most 1,536 input dimensions.
- Even allowing both coefficient triples and direct decoder access to both provides at most 3,072 scalar coordinates, below 4,608. This holds for affine encoders with arbitrary decoders, and separately for rational encoders with rational decoders.
- A decoder reading only five product blocks has only 2,560 scalar coordinates, a deficit of 2,048. This holds even for nonlinear rational decoding.

The rational result follows from `K(x)=K(Fx) subset K(E(x))` and transcendence degree; equivalently the generic Jacobian chain rule gives the same obstruction. Decoder denominators must remain nonzero after substitution, and all information depending on the selected payloads must be counted. Other independent dirty coordinates can be adjoined to the base field, avoiding an invalid zero-valued helper slice. The six boundary controls illustrate legal birational recovery, lost scale and an identically vanishing denominator; the written proof establishes the general theorem.

These are explicit interface restrictions. Five child calls in an arbitrary circuit do not imply them. Retained productive inputs, bypasses, wider coefficients or a different recursive primitive change the contract; dimension deficits are not native-cost or child-count lower bounds. No implementation or kappa improvement is claimed.

A constructive alternative is also checked: the first eight maps equal `I_8 tensor T_[459]`, realized by the same frame on 12 bits with 4,096 payload coordinates. Its Fourier rank remains 1; this does not establish a unit-priced rank-eight child. Its larger payload and complete native invoice remain open.

Base is freshly fetched canonical main `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90`, priority revision 6. Only `research/selected-toom3-typed-block` is added. Exact package commit is `251aba3a98e6eae2e2dd26c954aa0d1b2069cd4c`.

body:

The proof pairs local-ring projector geometry with time-unrolled circuit dependency. For n=64f, output address e_n cannot depend on any source bit with leading index n−1 when l<n. A valid all-class rank-seven projector on indices57..63, with arbitrary unit ancestor weights, requires precisely that dependency. Add a source-pinned exact search of latent-channel basis changes for the rank-34 P112 scalar fit in PR #3335. The scalar fitting matrix stays exactly fixed; each resulting term is priced on the complete source and reader plane spans under the inherited one-total pairing-rank tariff.

This is a scoped algebraic screen. It does not construct a physical decoder or establish a new supplier or κ.

## Result

- 19,683 signed-ternary matrices include 11,808 invertible over Q and realize 396 distinct source/inverse-reader support maps.

body:

Extends the exact two-plane decoder screen from binary coefficient values to generic rational coefficients. It enumerates all 65,536 4x4 support matrices, retains the 37,823 structurally nonsingular ones, and derives each generic inverse support from the perfect-matching condition on its 3x3 cofactors. A supplementary exact C11 census exhausts all `3^16 = 43,046,721` matrices with entries in `{-1,0,1}`. Of these, 27,947,520 are invertible. Every one of their inverse-support signatures is among the same 439 generic signatures; the signed coefficient values add no new support pattern. `TERNARY-SCREEN.txt` contains an exact matrix witness for each signature, and the Python verifier validates every witness and automatically recompiles/replays the full census when a C11 compiler is available.

We price all 439 signatures on all 1,540 pairs of certified planes (676,060 cases). It excludes neither rational specializations outside `{-1,0,1}` with cofactor cancellation, overcomplete decoders, mixing three or more planes, coefficient scaling overhead, changed multi-array primitives, nor physical routing/restoration. title: Research: exact Toom-3 five-product profile screen
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Constructs and verifies the exact five-product Toom-3 factorization for multiplying degree-two polynomials. The verifier reconstructs the rational interpolation map and checks all nine input monomial pairs.

A hypothetical block replacing nine selected rank-one recursive products with five saves four rank-one units. On the pinned complex profile, 64 realized blocks would clear the task card's five-percent local-ceiling gate; 210 would move the complex-side transfer cap above 0.002. At 254 hypothetical blocks, the local complex-side ceiling is [0.002086688163384, 0.002086688163385], corresponding to a local κ cap near 0.002082342962972. The selected forward and backward traces each contain 254 disjoint groups of nine rank-one climbs eligible under the phase-local movement model from #1817.

These are screening results, not a selected-provider construction: no group is bound to Toom coefficient inputs or outputs, and copies, scratch, dirty-state restoration, precision and native hosting remain unpriced. A direct scalar schedule costs 19 additions and 13 rational scales per hypothetical block.

This PR records a useful partial result and a negative global result. Under the retained transfer, the unchanged bit provider caps overall κ at 0.001730427469824, so the Toom-3 complex-side screen alone cannot reach overall κ > 0.002. Selected κ remains 0.001672660197076918. No new κ or supplier claim is made.

Base: freshly fetched canonical main `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90`. Task `complex-rank-shape-decoder`, **changed scope** to screen a five-product bilinear convolution factorization and its selected-profile effect.

PR #3895 (head `2e969106d82a7e53ee3a22580653521b4876cc6b`) remains an open draft for a two-root E8 rank-16 decoder; it does not bind a Toom-3 convolution block. This screen also differs from the diagonal rank-16 batching in #1779 and dependency-window model in #1817, and extends the two-coefficient Karatsuba screen in Discussion #1987. The replay checks the rational identity, all nine basis products, negative controls, selected-source pins and event schedule, exact profile-ceiling brackets and the unchanged bit-side cap. Publication-byte and source-history checks passed for commit `23bb4de61d629e3f103a65baa7882b34042ab10f`. No supplier cold replay, native compiler replay or Lean proof is claimed.

title: Construct a P104 dyadic tensor code and price repeated Gram stages

title: Prove P112 six-dimensional incidence floor and exclude two literal C5 callers
body:
Two literal historical C5 callers have total support budgets of 156 and 148. This package proves that eleven pieces spanning six P112 code dimensions need at least **164 support incidences**, excluding `5^10,7` and `5^9,6^2` with margins **8 and 16** over every characteristic-zero field. Their quotient dimension is five under the explicitly inherited second generalized-weight bound.

The new argument pairs generalized Hamming weights with root-matroid fibers and singleton/pair incidence. A common-zero correction raises the naive 152 floor to 158; pair incidence strengthens it to `164 + 4z`, where `z` coordinates vanish on the same six-dimensional code subspace. It permits arbitrary coefficients, cancellations and dependent pieces in the general lemma. Actual caller pieces retain their original independence hypotheses.

Evidence:

Screens whether mixing two certified matched planes through any invertible 4x4 `{0,1}` encoder and its exact rational inverse lowers the inherited F2 pairing-rank copy invoice. Every pair has minimum invoice 8, equal to four separate rank-two messages; there are zero strict improvements.

This is a complete negative result for the finite four-message, two-plane binary-basis subfamily. It does not exclude arbitrary rational or complex encoders, overcomplete factorizations, mixing three or more planes, a changed multi-array primitive, or physical routing/restoration.
